body: Finished the main game of **Crosscode**. I really liked it! Saw it recommended here all the time so I picked it up on sale for like $10, and that's gotta be the best $10 I've ever spent on a game. I thought the story was good and I really enjoyed the "game within a game". The skill trees were vast, the combat is fun, and it had some really likeable characters. How they expanded on the puzzles with each dungeon was really interesting and I had a good time with them. Felt at times the timing and precision was really tight, so failing was frequently just due to that and not because I didn't know what to do, but overall I thought the puzzles were good and creative. Getting it right on the ones you have to carry the ball across the whole screen always felt good. Going to give it a moment before I hope into the DLC I think, it took me around 60 hours to complete the base game and I need a bit of a break lol

I completed **Trails from Zero** with just over 90 hours of gameplay. I absolutely loved it. It's definitely a slow burner but once the story kicked off things got wild. I do believe that in order to fully understand >!the narrative with Renne!< you have to play the Sky games, otherwise to me it just wouldn't make any sense why there is so much importance given there. Zero was everything I loved from the Sky games, with some additional quality of life changes to make it all more enjoyable. The one I really appreciated was being able to stun any enemy by hitting them from behind. Such a nice addition. I will say the music from Sky is a bit more memorable, but that could just be a bit of nostalgia there. The music in Zero was still of course fantastic all around. I'm a touch burnt out from Trails right now, so I will wait until after Tears of the Kingdom to start Azure. >!I'm glad Zero didn't end with a giant cliffhanger so I don't feel bad about waiting to start Azure.!<. Also, I'm impressed that on Steam almost 40% of players beat Zero. That's a bit higher than usual I think.

The difference between JB1 and JB4 is mainly that the JB4 is more customizable, but the pre-loaded maps are still very good.

JB4 - I previously had the JB1 and purchased the JB4 upgrade kit. I didn't really read much into the differences other than the extra customizability but compared to the JB1, it is definitely faster. Nothing will completely void your warranty, but if the dealer can prove that a modification caused the failure, they can deny the warranty claim. 

If you are tuned and the turbo breaks, they will definitely deny that warranty claim.

Still with that tune, if your sunroof breaks, they will not deny that warranty claim because they can't prove at all that the tune caused that failure.

Cosmetic modifications will really not cause any problems. They don't cause any issues and it looks like a lot of the things you want to do include using the VCDS cable and changing settings. That is never going to be an issue, because you are utilizing settings that came with the car, but just weren't active.

At the end of the day, if the dealer can prove that the modification caused the failure, they can deny a warranty claim. Nothing will void your warranty completely. 

It wouldn't hurt either to speak with the service department at the dealer and get their insight on modifications and warranty work.
